_comment: Hand-maintained, unlike expectations.json which MigrationFixtureTool writes. The fixture database is at Flyway
version fixtureFlywayVersion; every newer migration in core/src/main/resources/migration runs when
DatabaseMigrationSystemTest starts the core with it and needs at least one check here, which
MigrationFixtureFlywayExpectationsTest (core) enforces. Each check runs its SQL through
/internalapi/debuginfos/executesqlquery against the migrated H2 2.4 database before the test makes any new
searches, and compares the rows (without the header, null for SQL NULL) with expectedRows.

4.sql: SELECT COLUMN_NAME, DATA_TYPE, CHARACTER_MAXIMUM_LENGTH FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS WHERE TABLE_SCHEMA = 'PUBLIC' AND TABLE_NAME = 'INDEXERUNIQUENESSSCORE' AND COLUMN_NAME IN ('OBSERVATION_ID', 'RECORDED_AT', 'DATA_VERSION') ORDER BY COLUMN_NAME

4.description: The legacy uniqueness score rows were kept
4.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM INDEXERUNIQUENESSSCORE WHERE OBSERVATION_ID IS NULL

SELECT INDEX_NAME FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.INDEXES WHERE TABLE_SCHEMA = 'PUBLIC' AND INDEX_NAME IN ('ISRO_INDEXERSEARCH_RESULT_INDEX', 'ISRO_SEARCH_RESULT_INDEX', 'IUS_OBSERVATION_INDEXER_INDEX') ORDER BY INDEX_NAME
SELECT SEQUENCE_NAME FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.SEQUENCES WHERE SEQUENCE_SCHEMA = 'PUBLIC' AND SEQUENCE_NAME = 'INDEXERSEARCHRESULTOCCURRENCE_SEQ'

5.sql: SELECT DATA_TYPE, CHARACTER_MAXIMUM_LENGTH FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS WHERE TABLE_SCHEMA = 'PUBLIC' AND TABLE_NAME = 'INDEXERSEARCH' AND COLUMN_NAME = 'ERROR_MESSAGE'

6.sql: SELECT DATA_TYPE FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS WHERE TABLE_SCHEMA = 'PUBLIC' AND TABLE_NAME = 'INDEXERSEARCH' AND COLUMN_NAME = 'RESPONSE_TIME'

7.description: SEARCH got the age and size criteria, empty for the existing searches
7.sql: SELECT COLUMN_NAME, DATA_TYPE FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS WHERE TABLE_SCHEMA = 'PUBLIC' AND TABLE_NAME = 'SEARCH' AND COLUMN_NAME IN ('MIN_AGE', 'MAX_AGE', 'MIN_SIZE', 'MAX_SIZE') ORDER BY COLUMN_NAME

7.description: The existing searches have no criteria
7.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM SEARCH WHERE MIN_AGE IS NOT NULL OR MAX_AGE IS NOT NULL OR MIN_SIZE IS NOT NULL OR MAX_SIZE IS NOT NULL
SELECT COLUMN_NAME, DATA_TYPE FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS WHERE TABLE_SCHEMA = 'PUBLIC' AND TABLE_NAME = 'SEARCH_SELECTED_INDEXERS' ORDER BY COLUMN_NAME

8.description: Only the 3 of the fixture's 50 search results a download references were kept
The downloads reference the new sequential IDs and the old IDs became the hashes
8.sql: SELECT r.HASH, r.TITLE, i.NAME FROM INDEXERNZBDOWNLOAD d JOIN SEARCHRESULT r ON r.ID = d.SEARCH_RESULT_ID JOIN INDEXER i ON i.ID = r.INDEXER_ID ORDER BY r.HASH

SELECT INDEX_NAME FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.INDEXES WHERE TABLE_SCHEMA = 'PUBLIC' AND TABLE_NAME = 'SEARCHRESULT' AND INDEX_NAME IN ('SEARCHRESULT_HASH_INDEX', 'SEARCHRESULT_FIRST_FOUND_INDEX', 'UKFTFA80663URIMM78EPNXHYOM_INDEX_C') ORDER BY INDEX_NAME

8.description: The foreign keys from and to SEARCHRESULT were recreated
8.sql: SELECT CONSTRAINT_NAME, TABLE_NAME FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLE_CONSTRAINTS WHERE TABLE_SCHEMA = 'PUBLIC' AND CONSTRAINT_TYPE = 'FOREIGN KEY' AND CONSTRAINT_NAME IN ('FKR5G21PDW3HHS1SEFVJY30TGMI', 'FKR5G21PDW3HHS1SEFKHD3HBDGL', 'ISRO_SEARCH_RESULT_FK') ORDER BY CONSTRAINT_NAME

9.description: No download with a user name is recorded as API (the fixture has no such download, so this only checks the end state)
9.sql: SELECT ACCESS_SOURCE, USERNAME, COUNT(*) FROM INDEXERNZBDOWNLOAD GROUP BY ACCESS_SOURCE, USERNAME ORDER BY ACCESS_SOURCE

10.sql: SELECT DATA_TYPE FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS WHERE TABLE_SCHEMA = 'PUBLIC' AND TABLE_NAME = 'INDEXERSEARCHRESULTOCCURRENCE' AND COLUMN_NAME = 'ID'

11.description: The sequences V2 started at 30000000000 restarted at 50, as the fixture's tables only have negative IDs
11.sql: SELECT SEQUENCE_NAME, BASE_VALUE FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.SEQUENCES WHERE SEQUENCE_SCHEMA = 'PUBLIC' AND SEQUENCE_NAME IN ('IDENTIFIER_KEY_VALUE_PAIR_SEQ', 'INDEXER_SEQ', 'INDEXERAPIACCESS_SEQ', 'INDEXERAPIACCESS_SHORT_SEQ', 'INDEXERLIMIT_SEQ', 'INDEXERNZBDOWNLOAD_SEQ', 'INDEXERSEARCH_SEQ', 'INDEXERUNIQUENESSSCORE_SEQ', 'MOVIEINFO_SEQ', 'NOTIFICATION_SEQ', 'SEARCH_SEQ', 'SHOWNNEWS_SEQ', 'TVINFO_SEQ') ORDER BY SEQUENCE_NAME

12.description: Every sequence steps by 1 except SEARCHRESULT_SEQ, which keeps 50 for the pooled optimizer
12.sql: SELECT SEQUENCE_NAME, INCREMENT FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.SEQUENCES WHERE SEQUENCE_SCHEMA = 'PUBLIC' ORDER BY SEQUENCE_NAME
